feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, tools, and progression. It reads professionally and is well aligned to leadership roles, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently present a focused brand in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo with visible progression, relevant scale metrics, and concrete platforms/tools adds trust.  
- Good technical-commercial balance: combines strategy, editorial operations, web modernization, analytics, and multimedia in a way that suits senior digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome language: several bullets describe duties (“led,” “supported,” “developed”) without enough measurable business/user impact beyond traffic and platform size.  
- Fix style consistency: use parallel bullet punctuation and list style throughout; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; consider standardizing name casing from “Coleman DAVIS” to “Coleman Davis” unless intentional.  

No major misspellings found; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It would be sharper with a few concrete signals of scope and less overlap with the subtitle, competencies, and recent project details.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years’ experience building platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add scale from recent roles to increase impact, e.g. “Led modernization of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace the generic “Leads…” sentence with a results-oriented line: “Directs web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia programs that improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”
- Use parallel phrasing and consistent style: “AI-enabled user experiences” is strong; consider “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to align with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats multiple skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and prioritize strategic/enterprise-level strengths over task-level items.
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Multi-channel communications leadership” to better match seniority.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows, use “content discovery” instead of “content experiences” for clearer business value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening it or making it more category-like rather than descriptive.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with both Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it feel more additive and polished.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [thing] that [impact].”
- Replace weaker phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with “built for ongoing campaign expansion” or similar.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for variety.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; keep only if framed as concise portfolio highlights rather than restating duties.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented leadership entry. Tighten phrasing and foreground 2–3 highest-impact contributions, especially AI search, Drupal campaign builds, and org-wide systems/governance.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications systems modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, workflows improved, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search performance gains, or time saved.
- Example rewrite: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the NACo Director role; distinguish this item by emphasizing consulting scope, AI search, and hands-on Drupal/front-end execution.
- The microsite/toolkit work also overlaps with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel oversight bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management for a national association.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented: add growth, engagement, production volume, or efficiency metrics for newsletters/social if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a generic scope statement.
- Strengthen results language in later bullets: e.g., “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events and recurring video content” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting to improve executive visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the opening and prior NACo role; either add measurable results or cut.
- Video/programming language overlaps with earlier NACo entries; keep this version focused on studio build and organizational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads as support-oriented rather than outcome-driven. Tighten it to emphasize scope, ownership, and what expanded under your leadership before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands…”; “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and output.”
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and the footer project; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” repeats the Director role; keep this version focused on execution and workflow leadership, not broad channel oversight.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, executive-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy and modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this skills block to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than adding vague skill labels.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat almost verbatim from Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with “storytelling experiences” and editorial planning already demonstrated in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the platforms/technical areas most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped capabilities, not a long stack list: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Consider dropping or de-emphasizing older/less evidenced platforms here (e.g., WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) unless they are important for target roles; keep those in Technical + IT instead.
- Replace “technical execution” language with impact-linked phrasing where possible, e.g., “Drupal platform delivery,” “enterprise CMS modernization,” or “search and automation implementation.”
- If space allows, align to recent evidence: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow automation, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost exactly; topline skills should be broader and more selective.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and outcomes, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the strategic skills: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten phrasing and group related items: “Analytics infrastructure • KPI design • Executive dashboards • SEO & performance insights • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows, align with recent impact from NACo: “Analytics infrastructure & executive reporting” better reflects the 2022–2024 leadership role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the full tool list here if those tools already appear in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and outcomes-oriented rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Hybrid Events**
- Tighten and elevate the bullets to:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio systems  
- Virtual event production and technical coordination
- If space allows, add one stronger qualifier such as **enterprise** or **broadcast-quality** to signal scale.
- Consider dropping “editing” if Premiere Pro already appears in Technical + IT; “post-production” sounds more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close enough that they should be consolidated or differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tighter and more senior-focused or add proficiency/context that reinforces recent Drupal-led work.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light qualifiers to show level without becoming a sentence: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, rename for precision: **CMS & Web Platforms** instead of **Web Platforms & CMS**
- Keep only platforms here; leave modernization, APIs, automation, and AI search in other technical sections

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats the **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; consider deleting one or making this version platform-only and the topline version capability-focused.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects, so avoid overloading this item with extra Drupal detail.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent work and grouping older/basic skills more tightly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, jQuery**
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior candidate.
- Put the strongest, more current implementation tools first; move **jQuery** to the end so it reads as legacy familiarity, not a primary stack.
- If accurate, consider replacing one generic term with a sharper capability: **REST API integrations**, **serverless scripting**, or **deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates **“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery”** and **“API integrations”** already listed under Topline Skills.
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** unless you specifically use it for implementation-heavy tagging architecture.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so tighten and frame around business use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If true, add a light qualifier to show depth: **Built and managed workflow systems using Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; coordinated delivery through Jira, Asana, Trello, and Basecamp**
- Consider dropping one weaker/older platform if space is tight; prioritize tools tied to recent work and automation impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells your email-platform leadership. It should signal enterprise-scale campaign/communications operations without repeating achievements already covered in NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers rather than just listing tools: **Enterprise email campaign delivery • newsletter operations • audience segmentation • member communications**
- Keep it concise and platform-focused; if one tool was only lightly used, move it later or remove it.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like “tens of thousands of subscribers” here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item specifically about email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills section. In Technical + IT, make it more tool-focused and tighter.

Suggested edit
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Remove **Dashboarding**; it’s a capability, not a tool, and is already implied by Power BI/Looker Studio.
- Consider replacing **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if you want this section to stay platform/tool-oriented; keep SEO in competencies or experience bullets instead.
- If accurate, add one advanced implementation tool only if used recently (e.g., **KPI reporting**, **conversion analysis**, or **funnel analysis** belongs elsewhere, not here).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep one strategic and one purely technical.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid repeating extra generic terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” or concrete outputs from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten management language: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate,” if accurate.
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this role as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; specify what changed or omit.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and novelty: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Keep the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest/stakeholder coordination, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid broad claims about leading digital strategy here, since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item currently reads generic and overlaps heavily with stronger multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities at a higher-level skills or experience level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a pure tools list: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
- If you want light context, use one concise label: **Adobe Creative Suite (Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator)**
- Remove “Livestream studio workflows” and “Podcast production” from this item; they are capabilities, not tools.
